 Tatyana Ali Reacts to ‘Young and the Restless’ Recasting Her Role
 Michael Maloney 
 November 17, 2026, 2:37 pm 
 Comments 
 Exclusive
 Sean Smith/jpistudios.com 
 Tatyana Ali didn’t need directions to get to the Dancing With the Stars studio after being cast in the show’s 35 th season. The ABC competition series tapes on the same lot as The Young and the Restless , the CBS daytime drama on which Ali spent several years playing Roxanne “Roxie” Barrington.
 And now that the character of Roxie is returning to the show — now portrayed by Tetona Jackson , as TV Insider previously reported —we had to get Ali’s take on her character’s comeback. And did Y&R reach out first to ask her to return as Devon’s ( Bryton James ) former girlfriend?
 “I don’t think anyone [from the show] called,” Ali told us on the DWTS pressline, hastening to add, “but I’m sure Tetona is amazing!”
 Paul Skipper/jpistudios.com
 The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air star also took a moment to reminisce about her time in daytime, which spanned from 2007 to 2013 and earned her a Daytime Emmy nomination. “The years I had on Y&R were like a little family,” she recalled. “[Tetona] is going to have a ball with Devon and the Winters family. It’s truly a blessing!”
 Right now, Ali has her eyes on a different prize than a return to daytime. She’s hoping to advance through Tuesday’s semi-finals and make it to next week’s finale! While Jenna Dewan ( The Rookie ) and Valentin Chmerkovskiy had higher scores than Ali did with her pro partner, Jan Ravnik , the former duo was sent home, and Ali and Ravnik learned they were going to the semi-finals.
 Sean Smith/jpistudios.com
 Ali says she got philosophical while waiting onstage to find out if she and Ravnik were safe. “I left it all on the floor,” she said. “What will be, will be.”
 The actress-singer added that she couldn’t have imagined being paired with anyone other than Ravnik as her DWTS pro partner. “I have the best partner,” Ali raved about her instructor. “He is the best teacher. He is patient.
 “I feel so grateful,” Ali continued. “I’m so excited to have a chance to keep going. I feel gratitude. I’m very thankful.”
 Disney/Christopher Willard
 It’s not uncommon for couples with sentimental stories to advance further along in the dance competition series if they strike an emotional chord with voters. “The scores are close, but there’s the voting,” she pointed out.
 Viewers have responded to Ali’s story as a maternal health advocate. “I’ve been doing that work for seven years because of the experience I had giving birth to my son,” she explained. “It was very traumatic. I testified in Congress about the fact that Black women are dying at three to four times higher rates .” While she noted that maternal health issues are abysmal for everyone, she added that “our rates are higher.”
 Disney/Christopher Willard
 The actress says that she’s learned about her body by pushing it to limits each week on DWTS . “Somebody wrote in a comment [on a post] that ‘your body holds the score,’” Ali recalled. “That’s a part of what I’ve been experiencing during this, freedom in my body. A lot of women have been posting about things that I’ve said about my body or comment on it. I just felt like [my journey] might be something that resonates with other women.”

 Inside 'Y&R's New Era: A Secret Affair, Big Returns & a New Year's Eve Twist 
 Ali and Ravnik are set to perform two dances on Tuesday night. They’ll do a Waltz to “Open Arms” by Journey, and a Cha-cha-cha to “I Like It Like That” by Pete Rodriguez.
 Whether she wins or loses the coveted  Len Goodman Mirrorball trophy, Ali hopes her journey on the show leaves an impression on her supporters.
 “I would love to be able to elevate the work that I’ve been doing with this show, and with this vast audience,” she said. “It means a lot that it’s resonating with the audience because it’s my story and it’s what so many are going through. It’s hard to say. I want to bring everything and all of me to this space. As a performer, I hope people are getting something out of spending time with us.”
 Dancing With the Stars , Tuesdays, 8/7c, ABC and Hulu and Disney+
